description: Taxonomy for coding Australian health practitioner disciplinary decisions. Based on AHPRA notification categories, GMC UK fitness-to-practise categories, NZMC categories, and project research questions.

CLIN.name: Clinical competence
CLIN.definition: Deficiencies in clinical knowledge, skill, judgement, or care delivery that fall below the expected standard for the practitioner's profession and level of experience.
examples: Failure to diagnose a condition that a competent practitioner would have identified
CLIN.inclusion: Errors or deficiencies directly related to clinical care delivery, diagnosis, treatment planning, or clinical decision-making.
CLIN.exclusion: Prescribing-specific issues (code under PRESC). Communication failures during clinical encounters (code under COMM). Impairment-related clinical errors (code under both CLIN and IMPR).

CLIN_DIAG.name: Diagnostic failure
CLIN_DIAG.definition: Failure to diagnose, misdiagnosis, or delayed diagnosis of a condition.

CLIN_TREAT.name: Inappropriate treatment
CLIN_TREAT.definition: Treatment that is not clinically indicated, is contraindicated, or falls below accepted standards.
examples: Using outdated or discredited treatment methods

CLIN_ASSESS.name: Inadequate assessment
CLIN_ASSESS.definition: Failure to conduct an adequate clinical assessment, history, or examination.

CLIN_RECORD.name: Inadequate record-keeping
CLIN_RECORD.definition: Clinical records that are absent, incomplete, inaccurate, or do not meet professional standards.

CLIN_INFCON.name: Infection control failure
CLIN_INFCON.definition: Failure to maintain infection control or hygiene standards.
examples: Failure to follow hand hygiene protocols

CLIN_OTHER.name: Other clinical competence issue
CLIN_OTHER.definition: Clinical competence issues not captured by the above subcategories.
examples: Practising outside scope without appropriate training
Failure to maintain clinical competence through continuing education

PRESC.name: Prescribing misconduct
PRESC.definition: Inappropriate, excessive, or fraudulent prescribing, dispensing, or supply of medications, including failure to monitor patients on medication, prescribing or dispensing without adequate assessment, and self-prescribing or self-supply.
examples: Prescribing opioids without adequate clinical indication
Prescribing to family members or self
PRESC.inclusion: All matters primarily concerning prescribing practices, medication management, or drug supply.
PRESC.exclusion: Drug-related impairment of the practitioner (code under IMPR). Clinical decisions about non-pharmacological treatment (code under CLIN).

PRESC_OPIOID.name: Opioid prescribing
PRESC_OPIOID.definition: Inappropriate prescribing of opioid medications (Schedule 8 or equivalent).
examples: Prescribing opioids to known drug-seeking patients
Failure to use opioid prescribing monitoring systems

PRESC_BENZO.name: Benzodiazepine prescribing
PRESC_BENZO.definition: Inappropriate prescribing of benzodiazepines (Schedule 4 Appendix D or equivalent).

PRESC_OTHER_S8.name: Other Schedule 8 prescribing
PRESC_OTHER_S8.definition: Inappropriate prescribing of Schedule 8 substances other than opioids.

PRESC_GENERAL.name: General prescribing failure
PRESC_GENERAL.definition: Prescribing failures not specific to controlled substances.

PRESC_SELF.name: Self-prescribing or prescribing for associates
PRESC_SELF.definition: Prescribing medication for oneself, family members, or close associates.
examples: Prescribing for family members without proper clinical relationship

PRESC_MONITOR.name: Monitoring failure
PRESC_MONITOR.definition: Failure to appropriately monitor patients on medication.
examples: No blood monitoring for patients on warfarin
No follow-up for patients on lithium
Failure to review opioid patients regularly

BOUND.name: Boundary violations
BOUND.definition: Breaches of professional boundaries in the practitioner-patient relationship, including sexual, emotional, financial, and social boundary violations.
examples: Sexual relationship with a current patient
Accepting large gifts from a patient
Engaging in a business relationship with a patient
BOUND.inclusion: All matters involving inappropriate relationships or interactions between practitioner and patient/client that breach professional boundaries.
BOUND.exclusion: Communication failures that do not involve boundary crossing (code under COMM). Financial fraud not involving patients (code under FRAUD).

BOUND_SEXUAL.name: Sexual boundary violation
BOUND_SEXUAL.definition: Sexual contact, sexual relationship, or sexualised behaviour with a patient or former patient (where the therapeutic relationship has not clearly ended).
examples: Sending sexual messages to a patient

BOUND_EMOTIONAL.name: Emotional boundary violation
BOUND_EMOTIONAL.definition: Inappropriate emotional involvement with a patient, including dual relationships and emotional dependency.
examples: Becoming emotionally dependent on a patient
Excessive personal disclosure to a patient
Personal relationship with a vulnerable patient

BOUND_FINANCIAL.name: Financial boundary violation
BOUND_FINANCIAL.definition: Inappropriate financial dealings with a patient.

BOUND_SOCIAL.name: Social/digital boundary violation
BOUND_SOCIAL.definition: Inappropriate social or online interactions with patients.

IMPR.name: Impairment
IMPR.definition: The practitioner's ability to practise is impaired by a physical or mental health condition, substance use disorder, or cognitive impairment.
examples: Practising while under the influence of alcohol
Unmanaged mental health condition affecting clinical practice
Diverting drugs of dependence for personal use
IMPR.inclusion: All matters where the practitioner's health or substance use is a primary concern affecting their fitness to practise.
IMPR.exclusion: Prescribing misconduct that is not related to the practitioner's own substance use (code under PRESC). Dishonesty to obtain drugs for patients (code under FRAUD).

IMPR_SUBSTANCE.name: Substance use disorder
IMPR_SUBSTANCE.definition: Practitioner has a substance use disorder or is practising while affected by alcohol or drugs.
examples: Diverting Schedule 8 drugs from the workplace

IMPR_MENTAL.name: Mental health impairment
IMPR_MENTAL.definition: Practitioner has a mental health condition that impairs their ability to practise safely.
examples: Unmanaged psychiatric condition affecting clinical judgement
Practising during acute mental health crisis

IMPR_PHYSICAL.name: Physical health impairment
IMPR_PHYSICAL.definition: Practitioner has a physical health condition or cognitive impairment affecting their ability to practise.
examples: Physical disability affecting clinical skills without appropriate accommodation

IMPR_NONCOMPLIANCE.name: Non-compliance with health monitoring
IMPR_NONCOMPLIANCE.definition: Failure to comply with health-related conditions on registration or monitoring programs.
examples: Failure to attend required drug screening
Non-compliance with mental health treatment plan
Breach of health-related conditions on registration

FRAUD.name: Dishonesty and fraud
FRAUD.definition: Deliberate dishonesty, fraud, or deception in the practitioner's professional conduct, including Medicare fraud, falsification of records, and misrepresentation of qualifications.
FRAUD.inclusion: All forms of professional dishonesty, fraud, deception, or misrepresentation.
FRAUD.exclusion: Inadequate record-keeping due to poor practice rather than deliberate falsification (code under CLIN_RECORD). Financial boundary violations with patients (code under BOUND_FINANCIAL).

FRAUD_BILLING.name: Billing or Medicare fraud
FRAUD_BILLING.definition: Fraudulent billing, including billing for services not provided, upcoding, or Medicare fraud.
examples: Billing Medicare for services not rendered

FRAUD_RECORDS.name: Falsification of records
FRAUD_RECORDS.definition: Deliberate alteration, fabrication, or destruction of clinical or professional records.

FRAUD_QUALS.name: Misrepresentation of qualifications
FRAUD_QUALS.definition: Misrepresenting qualifications, registration status, or professional credentials.

FRAUD_RESEARCH.name: Research misconduct
FRAUD_RESEARCH.definition: Fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism in research activities.

FRAUD_OTHER.name: Other dishonesty
FRAUD_OTHER.definition: Other forms of professional dishonesty not captured above.
examples: Deceiving patients about diagnosis or prognosis for financial gain

COMM.name: Communication failures
COMM.definition: Failures in professional communication with patients, families, colleagues, or regulatory bodies, including failures to obtain informed consent, inadequate disclosure, and failure to respond to complaints.
examples: Failure to obtain informed consent before a procedure
Failure to notify or report as required
COMM.inclusion: All matters where communication failures are the primary conduct concern.
COMM.exclusion: Record-keeping failures (code under CLIN_RECORD). Dishonest communication (code under FRAUD). Boundary-related communication (code under BOUND).

COMM_CONSENT.name: Informed consent failure
COMM_CONSENT.definition: Failure to obtain adequate informed consent before treatment or procedures.
examples: Failure to explain risks and alternatives

COMM_DISCLOSURE.name: Inadequate disclosure
COMM_DISCLOSURE.definition: Failure to provide patients with adequate information about their condition, treatment, or outcomes.

COMM_NOTIFY.name: Failure to report or notify
COMM_NOTIFY.definition: Failure to make mandatory notifications or reports to regulatory bodies, employers, or relevant authorities.
examples: Failure to make a mandatory notification about a colleague
Failure to notify a notifiable condition
Failure to report to AHPRA as required

COMM_CONDUCT.name: Unprofessional communication
COMM_CONDUCT.definition: Rude, aggressive, intimidating, or otherwise unprofessional communication with patients, families, or colleagues.
examples: Verbal abuse of patients or staff

PROF.name: Professional conduct
PROF.definition: Breaches of general professional obligations and standards of conduct not captured by other categories, including failure to comply with conditions, advertising breaches, and practice management failures.
examples: Failure to maintain professional indemnity insurance
PROF.inclusion: General professional conduct matters, breach of registration conditions, advertising, practice management, and matters not fitting other categories.
PROF.exclusion: Clinical competence issues (code under CLIN). Communication failures (code under COMM). Boundary violations (code under BOUND).

PROF_CONDITIONS.name: Breach of conditions
PROF_CONDITIONS.definition: Failure to comply with conditions imposed on the practitioner's registration.

PROF_ADVERTISING.name: Advertising breach
PROF_ADVERTISING.definition: Misleading, deceptive, or non-compliant advertising of health services.

PROF_INSURANCE.name: Insurance or registration failure
PROF_INSURANCE.definition: Failure to maintain professional indemnity insurance or registration requirements.
examples: Practising in a restricted area without approval

PROF_SUPERVISION.name: Supervision failure
PROF_SUPERVISION.definition: Inadequate supervision of students, junior practitioners, or support staff.
examples: Failure to supervise as required by conditions

PROF_OTHER.name: Other professional conduct
PROF_OTHER.definition: Professional conduct issues not captured by other subcategories.
examples: Conduct bringing the profession into disrepute
Failure to cooperate with regulatory investigation

CANCEL.name: Cancellation
CANCEL.definition: Registration is cancelled (may include a non-review period).

SUSPEND.name: Suspension
SUSPEND.definition: Registration is suspended for a specified period.

CONDITIONS.name: Conditions
CONDITIONS.definition: Conditions are imposed on the practitioner's registration.

REPRIMAND.name: Reprimand
REPRIMAND.definition: A formal reprimand or censure is issued.

UNDERTAKING.name: Undertaking
UNDERTAKING.definition: The practitioner gives an undertaking (e.g., to restrict practice, undergo training).

NO_ADVERSE.name: No adverse finding
NO_ADVERSE.definition: Complaint dismissed, charges not established, or no adverse finding made.

OTHER.name: Other
OTHER.definition: Outcome not captured by the above categories (e.g., costs orders only, referral to another body, consent orders with non-standard terms).

PM.name: Professional misconduct
PM.definition: A finding of professional misconduct — the most serious finding, typically involving conduct that is substantially below the standard reasonably expected of a practitioner of an equivalent level of training or experience.
legislation_refs: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law s 5

UPC_SAT.name: Unsatisfactory professional conduct
UPC_SAT.definition: A finding of unsatisfactory professional conduct — conduct that is below the standard reasonably expected of a practitioner of an equivalent level of training or experience but does not amount to professional misconduct.
legislation_refs: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law s 139B (NSW)

UPC_GEN.name: Unprofessional conduct
UPC_GEN.definition: A finding of unprofessional conduct — professional conduct that is of a lesser standard than that which might reasonably be expected of the health practitioner by the public or the practitioner's professional peers.
legislation_refs: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law s 5

NO_FINDING.name: No finding
NO_FINDING.definition: No finding of misconduct or unsatisfactory conduct is made. Complaint dismissed or not established.

coding_rules.multi_label: Decisions may have multiple misconduct categories. Code all applicable categories.
coding_rules.primary_outcome: When multiple outcomes are ordered, the primary outcome is the most severe (lowest severity_rank).
coding_rules.primary_finding: When multiple findings are made across different charges, the primary finding is the most serious.
coding_rules.consent_orders: Code consent orders the same as contested orders — the outcome category is determined by what was ordered, not how it was reached.
coding_rules.appeals: Code the appeal outcome, not the original decision outcome. Note in the 'notes' field that this is an appeal decision.
coding_rules.interim_orders: Do not code interim (interlocutory) orders as final outcomes. If the only decision is an interim order, note this and code the interim outcome separately.
